name: VfB Stuttgart

ucl_2026_27.qualified_via: Bundesliga 2025/26 4th place (62 points); second UCL league-phase appearance after 2024/25

identity.playing_style: Sebastian Hoeneß took over in April 2023 with the club 18th, survived via the relegation play-off, finished runner-up in 2023/24 and has now delivered a DFB-Pokal win (2025), a Pokal final (2026) and two UCL qualifications. His Stuttgart prioritise ball dominance (averaging over 57% possession) with an intense, centrally focused press out of a 4-2-3-1 that morphs into 4-4-2/4-2-2-2. In 2025/26 they had the Bundesliga's second-best attack, a record 41 away goals, and a home record of 17-3-5 across all competitions; Deniz Undav scored 19 league goals (second only to Harry Kane) and 25 in all competitions.
principles: coach continuity and early contract extensions (Hoeneß to 2028)
develop-and-sell talent pathway (Woltemade 2025, Chema Andrés EUR 25m to Brighton 2026, Millot 2025)
reinvest in Bundesliga-proven 22-26-year-olds (Pejčinović EUR 25m, Sauer EUR 13m, El Khannouss obligation EUR 18m)
regional identity: Mercedes-Benz and Porsche as anchor investors
50+1 member-controlled AG with strong supervisory-board oversight
identity.club_character: Members' club (VfB Stuttgart 1893 e.V.) that spun off the professional team into VfB Stuttgart 1893 AG in 2017; the e.V. holds the majority under the 50+1 rule, with Mercedes-Benz and Porsche as minority strategic investors. Passionate Swabian fanbase (MHP Arena ~60,000), a demanding regional press (Stuttgarter Zeitung, kicker) but a board (CEO Alexander Wehrle, sporting director Fabian Wohlgemuth) that has backed the coach through dips.
identity.ownership: member-controlled (50+1) AG; minority stakes held by Mercedes-Benz Group and Porsche AG
identity.political_and_social_context: Publicly documented institution-level facts only: (1) The club's governance model (e.V. majority in the AG, corporate minority investors) has been the subject of repeated member debates and a highly publicised 2023-24 dispute between club president and AG board over Porsche's entry, resolved with Porsche's investment. (2) Stuttgart lost the 2026 DFB-Pokal final 0-3 to Bayern as defending champions. (3) Sold Chema Andrés to Brighton for c. EUR 25m (EUR 16m to VfB after Real Madrid's share) and Jovan Milošević to Braga, Lazar Jovanović to Udinese in summer 2026. No sponsor or political controversies surfaced in this session's sources.
identity.wage_structure: hierarchical but capped (no superstar salaries; senior internationals Undav, Stiller, Demirović at the top)
identity.transfer_policy: data-led develop-and-sell: buys under-25 Bundesliga-ready players with resale value, sells peak assets to England/Spain at EUR 25-40m, replaces internally (Seimen promoted to No.1 after Nübel's loan ended)

last_season_2025_26.ucl_result: Not in UCL 2025/26; UEFA Europa League: knockout-phase play-off beat Celtic 4-1 away / 0-1 home (4-2 agg), round of 16 lost 1-2 home / 0-2 away to FC Porto (1-4 agg)
last_season_2025_26.domestic_cup: DFB-Pokal finalist (lost 0-3 to Bayern München, 23 May 2026, Berlin)

strengths: Elite Bundesliga attack: second-best offence in 2025/26, record 41 away goals, Undav 19 league / 25 total goals and now tied to 2029.
Tactical clarity and continuity under Hoeneß (since April 2023, contract to 2028): possession-dominant with a coordinated central press.
Strong home form (17 wins, 3 draws, 5 defeats in all home games 2025/26) in a 60,000 arena; UCL home slate of Atlético, Brugge, Lille, Viking is manageable.
Smart squad refresh: Pejčinović, Sauer, El Khannouss and Prömel added while selling Chema Andrés for EUR 25m.
Recent European experience: Europa League last 16 in 2025/26 and a UCL league phase in 2024/25.
weaknesses: Goalkeeping is the big gamble: Nübel returned to Bayern and 20-year-old Dennis Seimen (one 2. Bundesliga season) is the declared No.1 for a UCL campaign.
European knockout record is poor - eliminated by Porto 1-4 on aggregate and out of the 2024/25 UCL league phase.
Sold their best young defensive midfielder (Chema Andrés); Stiller/Karazor now lack a natural successor.
Zagadou's long injury history and a thin verified centre-back list (Chabot, Zagadou) behind a high defensive line.
Squad list for 2026/27 only partially verifiable in-session (15 names) - depth players not confirmed.
